parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs federal-level universal exposures with a state-level pattern of restriction and weak recourse. Every visitor passes a national entry/document system that now records sex assigned at birth, instructs officers to refuse cases casting doubt on sex, and treats suspected misrepresentation as potential lifetime fraud ineligibility; national custody policies documented include hormone removal and abuse of trans detainees. The state adds no adult bathroom ban but restricts school facilities, bans minors' transition care outright (affecting a travelling minor and their guardian), excludes gender identity from hate-crime law, and layers a religious-freedom statute over patchy municipal protections. No organised state targeting of adult visitors is documented, and employment/municipal protections plus litigation contest the worst federal measures, but no remedy shown actually reverses the exposures. This sits at the elevated-risk level: universal, partially unremedied exposure without local facility bans or police campaigns.

entry_documents.exposure: National documents now record birth sex; officers instructed to refuse applicants where sex is doubted and to consider lifetime fraud findings; trans travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and strandings; visa case-note tagging; foreign governments issued trans travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; policy contested in court with an unresolved civil-liberties suit; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's passport/visa record interacts with state document rules and any later police or custody encounter, propagating a mismatch through the journey.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau policies since 2026 mandate haircutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; prisoner counts suppressed.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visitor detention (e.g. a document dispute escalating) routes into these national custody practices; placement follows birth sex in practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars congruent facility access in government-funded single-sex facilities; 4 states criminalise some use, with a documented arrest and men's-ward holding of a trans woman; this state restricts school facilities only — no adult statewide ban documented, though unshown sex-definition policies may affect access.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban; this state's adult exposure is not a mapped criminal ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules bind regardless of state; the state's K-12 ban governs a travelling minor at school-attached facilities.

care_services.exposure: Statewide ban on puberty blockers and hormones for minors, no phase-out, in force since July 2023 and upheld on appeal; federal orders framing minor care as 'mutilation' and proposed insurance bars; federal hospital-record subpoenas chill care-seeking.
care_services.protection: None documented for minors; adult care access not shown restricted in this state.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor loses continuity of care on arrival; a minor's records could trigger investigation exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal rhetoric ('mutilation', 'radical gender ideology') frames trans people as threats; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; 2013 religious-freedom statute gives services a refusal route; school-transition facilitation criminally prosecutable.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment ruling partially in force; 19 municipal ordinances; conversion therapy barred by 2024 executive order.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing at national level raises outing severity everywhere; state enforcement gaps mean street-level bias has no enhancement here.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban for minors statewide; school bathroom and sports bans; teachers facilitating social transition face prosecution directives; no phase-out for children in treatment.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion-therapy ban (2024); municipal protections in 19 cities; litigation continuing.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care interruption and, if the minor uses school-designated facilities, legal ambiguity; state rules also signal which federal enforcement the state welcomes.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gender identity excluded from state hate-crime enhancement; 2011 park beating shows enforcement ran through the sexual-orientation provision only; no state violence statistics provided.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling apply; police cooperated with federal agencies and obtained convictions in the documented case.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public hostility may be latent; recourse depends on municipal ordinances or federal law, unevenly.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented remedy reverses the passport policy, custody practices or care ban; several federal orders enjoined but core exposures operative; litigation unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Running legal-aid FAQ on documents; courts have blocked some orders; municipal protections in 19 cities.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Traveller exposure varies with which measures are in force and location; adult facility use, detention placement, and app/enforcement practice in this state remain undocumented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: both feature a universal facility/document exposure without remedy and no general criminalisation of adult trans presence. Here the exposure is split between federal entry-document screening and custody rather than a single state bathroom rule, and this state lacks an adult public-building ban, slightly softening local scope while federal custody harm is worse than 0.45-A's record.

Less safe than 0.55-B: that province has no universal rule, only uneven service hostility with partial remedies. Here universal federal measures (document sex rules, entry refusal lever, custody policies) reach every traveller, and the minors' care ban is a categorical exclusion, outweighing 0.55-B's frictions.

Materially below 0.75-C, which has documented traditional acceptance, a dead-letter statute, and working court remedies. Here there is no comparable acceptance record, an active minors' care ban, excluded hate-crime coverage, and federal custody abuses with no shown relief; open questions are outweighed by documented universal exposures.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime the traveller encounters is federal-first: entry screening applies a birth-sex document standard with a refusal/fraud lever, federal facilities and custody carry documented harm, and no shown remedy reverses these — the state layer adds the minors' care ban, school facility and sports restrictions, excluded hate-crime coverage and a religious-refusal statute, while offering only municipal protections and appellate employment rights. An adult alone faces the universal federal exposures and open custody questions; an adult with a trans minor faces categorical care interruption and investigation-adjacent framing. No organised local police targeting is documented, which keeps this out of the high-risk band, but the unremedied universal measures place it at the lower edge of elevated risk.
